text: You can vibe-code a website. I wanted to vibe-build something I could touch.
My dog's water bowl keeps going empty, and I keep noticing too late. I've been a product manager for thirteen years. I can barely code, and I have never studied electronics.
So I built this, and then I became its first user. I told it what I wanted, in one sentence, the way I'd say it to a person.

It read what I already own, searched its own parts catalog, and came back with a shopping list. Six parts, seventeen dollars, each one with what it does, why that one, and a link I can actually click.
And a warning I would never have thought to ask for: this sensor runs at five volts, the board's pins do not, so do not wire them straight together.
The parts arrived. I could not name a single object in the box.
So I took a photo and asked. It went through the pile and told me what each thing was, and which one was actually the controller.

Then the real barrier showed up. The guide says V C C. My screen says V D D. Same pin. Two naming conventions, decades old, both still alive. An expert's eye corrects it without noticing. I lost ten minutes.
That is why every part name in here is a link. One tap: a picture, the voltage, every pin, how to wire it, and the mistakes everyone makes with it.
When I was ready, it wrote the firmware, compiled it, and flashed it onto the board on my desk.

All of this runs on Nebius Token Factory. Nemotron 3 Super drives the loop: thirty tools, about a second per step. When something is flashed but doesn't work, it escalates to Nemotron 3 Ultra, which weighs power, wiring, logic levels and code together.

And it is never allowed to recall a pin number from memory. Every one has to come from the board's own profile. There is even a file in here listing every time this AI has been confidently wrong about hardware, and it has to re-read it before it answers me.
This is vibe building. In the real world, the light either comes on, or it doesn't. I have never studied embedded systems for a single day. If I could get here, so can you.
